item.title: (LSJ) How to get best ROI from Social Media?
item.content:encoded:
(LSJ, Editor in Chief, @lsj2030), Social media is based on Customer Relations Management  (CRM) principles. To measure Return of Investment (ROI) for Social Media is a calculus of marketing mix costs invested in to Social Media Launches and Projects, and the following  sales operations Profits and growing Brand Value of its brand mix.

When a company decides to invest in to social media it needs long-term strategy and commitment. Social Media is important tool for modern Marketing Management Strategy. How does this work?

1. Social Media opens and strengthens the FLOW between your Customers and your PRODUCTS, BUSINESS, and PEOPLE. The Social Media Ecosystems sustain the brand value.

It results in improved Customer Satisfaction, improved Acceptance Rate for your new  and old PRODUCTS and strengthens your BRAND Promise and later  BRAND Value. 

YES, Social Media will finally improve your Sales and raise ROI. Finally. But there is more.

Social Media marketing differs somewhat from Direct Marketing (DM). It is based on relations built to your customers, competitors, partners, and friends, brands, signs, products, ideas, communities, bands, etc.

Mass Marketing and Direct Marketing is  fundamentally more aggressive based on pushing the message to the prospect buyer. Customer Relations Marketing is more indirect, more friendly activity, where customer retention of your updates reflect and builds the relationship. with your Social Media Promise and the customer. Ofcourse Social Media services like Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn.com, Google Buzz offer good tools for selected messages to be sent segmented audience, which can be used alike of Direct Marketing.

ACTION ITEM 1: -> Start Social Media Project today, starting with one of the best brands in your company.

2. Learn from the Feedback of the Customer

When your first project is and running, The Customer up gives to your company the Feedback to change and to improve your activities and operations. It is your social media partner/operations excellence to get really rich feedback through competitions, events, games, challenges, questions, direct messaging. i.e The Social Media marketing Mix. It is up to your business to pivot those changes to your products and operations.

ACTION ITEM 2: -> Start changing your Business from what you learn daily from your customers.

3. Personal Social Media Road-Map

As a beginning with Social Media activities, you end up hunting all new friends and services. This is important phase to learn and to understand the possibilities of Social Media. Expect as SME that this takes one to two to three years minimum. Spend all the time you have building connections. Second alternative is hire someone that has gone through three to five years already.

After good time spent with FB and Twitter, and adding all of those 66k contacts ( thanks @crhissvoss for the example), You need to open one-to-one discussions, debating, finding joint possibilities, sales, projects, meetings, etc. Try not to look arrogant (thanks for tip by @guykawasaki). Try to listen, even if you are an Engineer like me, whose first life time went in the Computer Room checking green lights, not with the people.

4. Delivering Mind Share before Market Share. Social media is the tool to give your PRODUCT and your COMPANY better visibility, a Mind Share if you will. Only Old Tool-Tim sells the TOOL with Market Share in mind.

I see many times see consultants that pretend to advice me Social Media as the PRODUCT. How many of us sells Facebook services successfully? Or Twitter promoted tweets? OK, I see hands raising, but my point is it is easier to concentrate to products of your customer, and create a solutions for those, instead of the selling only the tool. Mind share vs. market share.

5. Social media is long-term Partnership, a true Lifetime friend.

Use it wisely, and it will make you connect with the people you deserve. I have found that 9 out of 10 people in what ever social media I want to contact with have a friendly face for me. That does not say, that they immediately want to invest to my companies. But, overall social media does what it promises. It connects you and ecosystems. And that is a lot altogether.

“Listen carefully, I will say this only once”

“The best way of building relationship marketing with social media is to listen carefully and answer questions, emails, and commenting blogs﻿”@blogtheristo @foursquare Risto P

item.title: (LSJ) Social Video will boost the sales and affect pricing in eCommerce
item.content:encoded:
The Social Video will revolutionize the business talk. Use of video will replace flash and other graphical solutions. Why? It is the fastest and most natural way of receiving and producing business information.

Sharing videos and creating their own videos is the foundation of Generation Y and youngsters living.

 

Remember matchbox videos?

 

Back in 1996 I remember first time downloading CNN news clips from the source to a browser’s ‘matchbox’ sized window. The  ISDN  (64k) bandwidth could not deliver better quality. This situation lasted over a decade, as video streaming was something out of my reach.

Today, even mobile internet  (3G) offers bandwidths that deliver social video 10 times faster than was possible 1996. This changes the picture.

How does Social Video change business?

The first function that is likely changing is Sales and Promotion of products in eCommerce. Buying a product before seeing it in action through video stream will become a ‘strange’ behaviour. We want to see the product, and when possible company representatives to ‘pitch’ their products.  We want to learn how the product is used before we buy it. And we want to see if there is pitfalls in that particular  product that we should know before valuing the deal buy/no buy.

Price raises with praising customers that are engaged

Praise for your product friends will create new possibilities to the next version of your product.  Think about the success story of IPhone.  Huge success in IPhone 3 ffects the pricing possibilities of coming Iphones immediately. Companies need to reflect pricing as their product is raised or lowered in the ranks to optimize profitability. Ofcourse market demand remains is the biggest factor for price formulation, but with social video the prize range can be wider. Engaging all Iphone fans means pricing possibilities for  the version of IPhone

Friends engage me and maybe also decide what I like

Furthermore, with social video it is important to see and hear what friends who have tested the product think of it. The word of mouth turns to video streams where friends are having fun with the product (f.e. how easy it is to use Facebook in IPhone). Also more formal  information reaches me f.e.  how unknown friends rated by other product users. Seeing makes me believer.

Lifetime Studios produce quality eCommerce solutions. Every product created  has the possibility to include social video, flahs, quicktime, f.e., along with Facebook Share and Tweet this button. Are your company ready take 24 / 7 challenge in the markets? If so, you propably will continue to success in the next wave of internet.

 

From selling Ideas, Opinions, Solutions, Products, and so on to engaging with Social Videos

The value chain becomes experience chain where social video provides crucial information about your product. The market opinion.. is engaged in Facebook Video page or Youtube.

 

I want share one good example of opinion selling, and engaging me to act.

In this video stream embedded opinions are sold with a solution that seems to irresistable and straight forward. In a three minutes SAP ideas are sold so that I understand and can act.

from SAP Community page: “Business ByDesign is SAP’s solution for fast-growth companies with modules for business analytics, financial management, accounting, CRM, supply chain, and more. Just choose the modules you need when you need them. SAP will host ByDesign for you so that you can focus on getting ahead of your competition and growing your business.”

Marato Barcelona Running Team 28.10.2010 – 12.3.2011

Espoolainen maratonkoulu, jossa tavoitteena on aktiivisen juoksuharrastuksen kehittäminen. Päätavoitteet ovat osallistuminen Länsiväyläjuoksuun 17.4.2011 ja Barcelonan maraton 6.3.2011. Ensimmäinen tapaaminen ja ilmoittautuminen on 28.10.2010 kello 17.00–20.00 Esport Areenassa.

Tule mukaan jos olet

  • Juoksuharrastusta aloittamassa. Juoksukisaan valmistautuminen.
  • Juoksuharrastusta kehittämässä (juossut jo esim. 10km ,½ maraton, maraton). Ajan, tekniikan, juoksuharjoittelun kehittäminen.

MaratoBarcelona 2011 Running Team Training Location from Blogtheristo @LifetimeStudios on Vimeo.

A short video about the whereabouts of the training location.

Juoksukoulun ohjelma

  • Alkutestaus 28.10.2010 alkaen (arvo 50 €) ja sen pohjalta laadittu henkilökohtainen ohjelma (arvo 50 €).
  • Ohjatut harjoitukset tehdään Esport Areenan sisäradalla 30.9.2010 alkaen torstaisin klo 18.00, viikoilla 43, 44, 45, 46, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
  • Luentoja 2 kpl. Harjoitusviikkoja 20 12.3.2011 saakka.
  • Omaehtoinen harjoittelu ohjelman mukaisesti Esport Arena / ulkona / Sali.
  • Pitkä lenkki yhteisharjoituksena 1krt. viikossa Espoon keskuspuiston lähistöllä.
  • Juoksun sisäharjoituksiin tarvitset Esport pääsylipun 6,0 € (kortilla 10 Kurt).

  • Länsiväyläjuoksun osallistumismaksu kuuluu hintaan.

Sisältö ja Hinnat

½ Maraton-juoksupaketti                                      hinta 340 €              

Suorituskykytesti 1 kpl (Keijo), henkilökohtainen ohjelma (Ilkka), ohjatut harjoitukset yht. 8+1 krt. Mahdollisuus osallistua yhteislenkkeihin. Luennot aloitus, ravitsemus, ja fysio,  kortin Leppävaaran Sisun valituille ryhmäliikuntatunneille (Sonja), Osallistumisen Länsiväyläjuoksuun 17.4.2011 (LeSi), tuotealennukset tiimin verkkokaupasta, Facebook-palvelut.

Maratonpaketti Marato Barcelona 2011

Tavoitteet

maratonia, satoja muita kestävyysurheilutapahtumia.

Testaukset

FYSIO- SPORT PETÄKOSKI OY

SPORT- SEKTORIN KESTÄVYYSTESTIT

1 KESTÄVYYSTESTIN ESITIETOLOMAKE JA PERUSMITTAUKSET

Ennen kestävyystestin suorittamista testattava täyttää esitietolomakkeen, jossa kysytään terveyteen ja liikuntaan liittyviä kysymyksiä. Tämän avulla voidaan huomioida testituloksessa erinäisiä muuttujia ja arvioidaan testin soveltuvuus. Esitietolomakkeen tiedot ovat salassapidon alaisia eikä niitä tulla esittämään tai käyttämään missään yhteydessä. Ennen kestävyystestin suorittamista mitataan perusmittauksina pituus ja paino. Näiden avulla saadaan arvioitua tarkemmin kestävyystestissä mitatut muuttujat ja suorituskykyarvio. Lisäksi arvioidaan painon ja pituuden suhde sekä seurataan harjoittelun vaikutusta painon hallintaan.

2 KESTÄVYYSSUKKULAJUOKSU

Kestävyyssukkulajuoksutesti (tunnetaan myös piip - testinä) ja suoritetaan yhtäjaksoisena juoksuna 20 metrin matkalla edestakaisin minuutin välein kiihtyvällä vauhdilla siten, että toinen jalka ylittää merkkiviivan äänimerkin määräämällä vauhdilla. Mikäli suorittaja ehtii merkkiviivalle ennen äänimerkkiä, niin etenemistä saa jatkaa äänimerkin jälkeen. Jos äänimerkki tulee ennen kuin suorittaja on ehtinyt merkkiviivalle asti, niin suorittaja juoksee viivalle asti ja jatkaa etenemistä. Kestävyyssukkulajuoksutesti keskeytetään, kun suorittaja myöhästyy kolme peräkkäistä kertaa äänimerkistä. Kestävyyssukkulajuoksun etenemisvauhti kiihtyy minuutin välein. Kestävyyssukkulajuoksun etenemisnopeutta säädellään viheltämällä.

Kestävyyssukkulajuoksusta mitataan koko suorituksen ajalta sykereaktio, maksimisyke lyöntiä minuutissa (Lm) kokonaissuoritusaika (min, sek) ja etenemisnopeus (km/h). Kestävyyssukkulajuoksun testituloksen avulla voidaan arvioida maksimaalinen hapenotto (VO2max). Kestävyyssukkulajuoksun sykereaktion perusteella arvioidaan aerobinen suoritus, anaerobinen suoritus (vauhtikestävyys) ja maksimisuorituskyky. Kestävyyssukkulajuoksun kokonaisajan perusteella arvioidaan maksimisuorituksen kehittymistä.

Kestävyyssukkulajuoksutestit soveltuvat sellaisille henkilöille, jotka harrastavat säännöllisesti hengästymistä aiheuttavaa liikuntaa vähintään kaksi- kolme kertaa viikossa tai joilla on urheilutausta. Kestävyyssukkulajuoksu ei sovellu ortopedisistä vaivoista kärsiville henkilöille.

item.title: (LSJ) Workstyle revisited (based on writing of Robert Pease)
item.content:encoded:
What’s Your Workstyle?

December 28th, 2010 by Robert Pease

Robert defines Workstyle as follows:

 “New Workstyle?”

‘The New Workstyle blends the latest technologies and tools with our daily activities allowing us to accomplish more in both personal and professional endeavors, accelerate ideas of our own, and lead more productive lives.

Unlike workflow which is defined by scripted and static process for everyone to follow, workstyle is unique to the individual who calls upon information, technology, and connections as needed.’

 

Here are my Workstyle 2011 revisited charateristics:

1. Work Anywhere, anytime when needed.

2. Send and receive Streaming any direction. Video is becoming de facto communications channel for everything.

3. One delivers value, and focus on value creation rather technology.

4. Chosen Ecosystem is Cloud services interconnected. We at Lifetime Studios use Google Apps for Business, Huddle.com, LinkedIn.com, Twitter, Facebook, GIST, XING, among other. Are accounts are interconnected. Other similar Ecosystems can be gathered from Apps in the market that deliver similar Ecosystem(Technology independent).


5. Quality of personal Contacts (QoC) increases daily. Not just count friends but create more value with your (lesser) friends.


6. Team working daily for anything add value. Any document, picture, or meeting delivers more when shared with love.


7. Have focus on People. Leaving the office and meet people is the best communications strategy.


8. Balances his/hers processes (BPM/PPM). There is always time for a 60 minutes Running.


9. ‘Give and Go’ (get the ball back for scoring. Together based value chains). 


10. Keeps up learning new. What did you learn from this post?

 

Finally, kindly tell me, what kind of Workstyle do you live ?

Thanks Robert for the Original writing !

Thank you everyone for being a lifetime friend !

Risto

Update on 2011-06-10 14:40 by Editor in Chief, Lifetime Studios

Check out this updated version from Gist Blog:

http://blog.gist.com/2011/06/07/the-new-workstyle-leaving-the-old-behind/

item.title: (LSJ) Yrityssivut, Facebook, Google Plus, Intranet, Extranet Lifetime Oy:stä
item.content:encoded:
Tiesitkö että, Lifetime Studios on tuottanut Facebook sivuja jo vuodesta 2008? Tiesitkö että lifetime.fi sivut on olleet näkyvissä vuodesta 1996?  Aloitin Helsingin yliopistossa Multimediasovelluksen kehittämisen 1991. Sovellus pyöri yliopiston aulassa informaatiokioskissa. Tiesitkö että Lifetime Oy perustettiin 1989 taloushallinnon sovelluksen kehittämiseksi? 

Olen ollut mukana sosiaalisen median palvelujen tuotannossa jo vuodesta 2005. Aloitin Yahoo! -palveluilla tammikuussa 2005, ja Facebook tuli mukaan tuotekatalogiimme 2007. Blogia olen pitänyt vuodesta 2005, ja Lifetime Scope Journal aloitti Squarespace 3:lla joulukuussa 2006. Twitterissä olen ollut mukana vuodesta 2008 ja osallistuin mm. ensimmäiseen Twitter Developer Conferensiin 2008 (Chirp).  Google Apps for Business konsultointia olen tehnyt vuodesta 2010. Microsoft MCP tutkinnon suoritin 2001. Ylläpidettyjä Google Plus sivuja n. 50 kpl. Tutustumisen arvoinen: Google Apps for Business Signals (Google Plus).

Twitter for Developers

Ennen siirtymistäni yhteisö- ja verkkopalveluiden tuottajaksi toimin  15 vuotta tietohallintotehtävissä suurissa kotimaisissa ja kv. organisaatioissa. Koulutukseltani olen ohjelmistoinsinööri vm. 1991 sekä tuotantotalouden DI vm. 2007.

Lifetime Studios on viime vuosina toteuttanut useita merkittäviä Facebook ja markkinointikampanjoita ja sivustoja. Kysy lisää 0400 319 010 ja pyydä tarjous.

Ystävällisin terveisin, Lifetime Studios // Risto (tervetuloa verkottumaan kanssani Linkedin).

Luotettavaa kokonaispalvelua Lifetime Oy:stä

Lifetime Studios tuottaa yrityksellenne:

1. Nettisivut yritykselle 

Lifetime Studios tuottaa internet-sivunne maailman ehkä parhaimmalla palvelualustalla Squarespace.comilla. Squarespace.com Unlimited maksaa vain 16 dollaria kuussa ja antaa todella hienot ominaisuudet yrityksen verkkoviestinnän tyylikkääseen ja turvalliseen toteuttamiseen.

Yhdistä Squarespace Unlimited Lifetime Studiosin Professional Monthly ylläpitopalvelutuotteeseen, ja yrityksenne sivut ovat aina ajantasalla.

Eikä siinä vielä kaikki, palvelua on helppo laajentaa Lifetime Studiosin muilla tuotteilla eri sovellusalustoille ja tarpeille sopiviksi. Esimerkiksi Tuotemarkkinointi, verkkokampanjat, Brand Management, verkkokaupat, AdSense markkinointi, AdWords markkinointi, FacebookAds Markkinointi, LinkedIn Products, Squarespace Funnels, Cloud Computing, CRM, Asiakasrekisteri, 7P Marketing Strategy.

SquareSpace 6 skaalaa kaikki kuvat 7 eri kokoon joten kuvat näyttävät hienoilta eri alustoilla.

2. Facebook kotisivut yritykselle, tuotemerkeille, tuotteille

n. 2 miljoonaa suomalaista etsii tuotetiedot ja shoppailumahdollisuudet Facebookista.  Varmista mukanaolo Lifetime Studiosin kumppanina. Ylläpidämme n. 150 Facebook sivua (2012).

OpenGraph yhdistää tuotemerkit ja Facebook käyttäjät

3. Markkinointikampanjat Google Adwords ja FacebookAds alustoille

Rakennamme markkinointikampanjanne yhdistettynä sosiaalisen median palveluihin kuten Twitter, LinkedIn, Facebook, Google+, XING.  FacebookAds kampanjamme tavoittaa kaikki Facebookin käyttäjäryhmät. 

4. Google Apps for Business Platform on operatiivisesti toimiva ja hauska kumppani

Lifetime Oy palvelee Teitä kun haluatte varmistaa yrityksenne operatiivisen toiminnan tehokkaasti pilvipalveluin. Toimistoautomaatioalustana Google Apps for Business sisältää Google Corporation tärkeimmät sovellukset (gmail) ja kolmansien osapuolten laajan sovellustarjonnan. Teemme tuntityönä ylläpito- ja kehitysprojektinne nopeasti ja ammattitaidolla.

 

5. Lifetime Oy = Luotettavaa palvelua, kokemusta, kustannustehokkuutta, = menestystä

Pilvipalvelut (Google Apps for Business) + Nettisivut (SquareSpace + Facebook + Google+) + Kampanjat (Google Adwords + FacebookAds) + Operatiivinen osaaminen (Google Apps for Business) = Lifetime Studios Missio.

item.title: (LSJ) The all new Note App
item.content:encoded:
The Note app from Squarespace.com allows you to create notes and send them directly to a Blog within your Squarespace site

The Note app allows you to create notes and send them directly to a Blog within your Squarespace site, or to your email, Twitter, Facebook, Dropbox and Evernote accounts.

When you first open Note, an on-screen tutorial will walk you through some of the app functions and will leave you at the Note Editor.

Step 1 - Connect a Squarespace Account

Swipe to the left while viewing the Note Editor. Then, touch the + button next to Squarespace to connect your Squarespace account to Note.

Enter your Squarespace login credentials and touch the arrow to login to your account.

Select the site you want to use if you have multiple sites registered to your Squarespace 6 login.

Note: If you are using Squarespace 6, you will need to login using the email address for your Squarespace account. If you are using a Squarespace 5, you will need to login with your Squarespace account name. This guide explains how to know whether you are using Squarespace 5 or Squarespace 6.
Step 2 - Configure your Squarespace Account Options (Optional)

Once you've logged in to your Squarespace account, you can configure the Note options for this account.

You can configure these options for your Squarespace account:

Default: Note will send notes to your Squarespace site by default when a note is sent.
Sync: This will backup your notes to your Squarespace account. These notes will be accessible if you are using the Note on another device with this account. This is available specifically when using a Squarespace 6 account.
Publish To: Choose the Blog page where you want Notes added to your Squarespace site to appear.
Post Type: Choose to have your notes sent to your Blog as either a draft or published post.
Once you have configured these options as you'd prefer, touch the lines in the upper right corner to return to the Account Setup screen.

Note: You can touch the Squarespace icon at any time from this screen to change the Squarespace account you are using with Note.

Step 3 - Add Additonal Accounts (Optional)

Touch the + button next to the specific account(s) that you would also like to use with Note. You will then be prompted to link that account to Note.

Once you have added each account, you can configure the options for that account with Note. These will appear differently depending on the account you are adding to Note.

Email

Using an email address with Note will allow you to send notes directly to the address via email.

Default: Note will send notes to your email address by default.
Send Location: Note will include the location information from your device with the note once it is sent.
Subject Line: Choose whether the subject of the note will be either an excerpt of the note or add a custom prefix to appear before the excerpt in the subject of the note.
Dropbox

Using a Dropbox account allows you to send these notes as text files to your account.

Default: Notes will be sent to your Dropbox account by default when a note is sent.
Send Location: Note will include location information within the note when this is toggled on.
Separate Files: Choosing this option will allow Note to save each note sent to Dropbox as an individual text file.
Filename Date: This will include the date within the filename of the note. This is only available when the Separate Files option is turned on.
Append Date: Toggling this option on will add the date that the note was sent within the file for the note.
Twitter

Using a Twitter account will send your notes as tweets to your account.

Default: Note will be sent to your Twitter account by default when a note is sent.
Send Location: Notes sent to Twitter will include your location when this is toggled on.
140+ Character Limit: Choose whether notes will be sent when they exceed the character limit for Twitter. Note can split these into separate tweets or exclude these notes from being sent to your Twitter account.
Facebook

Using a Facebook account will send notes to your account as a wall post to appear within your timeline.

Toggling the Default option, will determine whether notes are sent to your Facebook account by default.

Evernote

Using an Evernote account will send notes to the notebook of your choice.

Default: Notes will automatically be sent to your Evernote account when this option is toggled on.
Notebook: Choose the specific notebook within Evernote to add your notes to.
Additional Services

From the account setup screen, swipe down, then touch the + button to add additional services that can be used with an email address.

You can also remove services simply by touching the red x next to each service.

Note: You can remove an account at any time by touching the Remove Account button at the bottom of each of the account settings screens. Confirm this by touching the Remove Account button a second time.

Step 4 - Add Notes

To compose a new note, swipe to the right from the Account Setup screen to reveal the Note Editor. Here, you can use the keyboard to type your note.

Once you're ready to send your note, swipe up on on your device to send your note.

This will send the note out to the services that you have configured as your default services.

Step 5 - View Your Sent Notes

From the Note Editor, swipe to the right to view your previously sent notes.

To delete a note, swipe your finger on the note to the right and tap the x icon.

Note: You can also delete multiple notes by selecting more than one at a time. To do this, swipe down while viewing your notes. You can then tap the notes you want to delete.
Step 6 - Send a Note to an Additional Account (Optional)

Tap a note you have previously sent if you would to send this note to another account. Then tap the icon for the service you want to send the note to.

Note: Only accounts that have been previously configured will appear when viewing a note.
Step 7 - Configure Note Settings (Optional)

Within the Settings for your device, tap Note to configure additional settings for the Note app.

item.content:encoded:
For many managers savings of 50 % per workstation is a good work. Here is how to do it.

Lifetime Studios Advisors will be there to help your organisation further in the Google Apps for Business deployment process Contact us.

 

1. Deploy Google Apps for Business

 10+ good reasons to deploy Google Apps for Business for your organisation.

Productivity

I need a productivity solution that’s easy to deploy and doesn’t require the ongoing maintenance of desktop software.

Scalability 

I want a solution that meets my needs today and automatically gets better over time.

Reliability

I need a productivity solution that I can rely on.

Collaboration

My employees need to collaborate seamlessly across organizational, geographical and linguistic barriers.

Team Work Capabilities

I want my employees to move faster without being slowed down by inflexible technology.

On the Road Mobile Office Productivity

My employees need to do more from mobile devices than just send emails.

IT managebility

My company employees needs to follow IT department rules and security policies. This saves time and money.

I want a simple licensing model that is cost-effective and predictable.

I want to spend half as much on IT as I do today.

 

Read more about Google Apps for Business Technology Benefits here.

2. Replace Workstations with Chromebooks

The Chromebook is a new computer that helps you get everyday things done faster and easier. It starts in seconds, has virus protection built-in, and runs your favorite Google apps plus thousands more. The Chromebook comes with leading Google products, like Search, Gmail, YouTube and Hangouts, so you can work, play, and do whatever you want, right out of the box. 

You can easily share it with multiple people- switching accounts takes seconds, and everyone gets their own files, apps and settings. And it’s simple to use. There’s no setup, and your files are automatically backed up in the cloud.

2.1 Samsung Chromebooks

At just 2.4 pounds, 0.7 inches thin, and with over 6.5 hours of battery life, the Samsung Chromebook can go anywhere you go. It’s built to stay cool, so it doesn’t need a fan and runs silently. It also includes 100GB of free Google Drive storage (for 2 years), a built-in webcam, and dual band Wi-Fi to make it easy to connect to wireless networks.

Order your Samsung ChromeBook here.

                     

 

2.2 Acer Chromebooks

Product features include (Source: Amazon Acer C7 Product Page)

  • The best of Google Chromebook Apps built-in: Google Search, Gmail with Hangouts, YouTube, third-party Google Drive Apps. 
  • You can work, play, and do whatever you want, right out of the box. Thousands of free apps in the Chrome Web Store, you can watch movies, play games, or get work done (if you really have to).
  • Easy to use The Acer C7 Chromebook is simple to use and stays up-to-date automatically. It boots-up in less than 20 seconds, never slows down, and requires almost zero setup or maintenance. 
  • All your apps follows your account when you need to change working device.
  • Great for entertainment Games and videos come alive with its 11.6” high definition display. You can also connect it easily to external monitors and displays with HDMI and VGA outputs and multiple USB ports.
  • Stay connected The Acer C7 Chromebook stays connected with dual band Wi-Fi. It also comes with 12 free Gogo Inflight passes so you can stay online even when you’re not on the ground. And Chromebook has offline apps for the rare times that you’re disconnected from the web.
  • A squabble-free family computer (almost) Easily switch between users in seconds. Everyone has their own files, apps, and settings. You never have to worry about anything getting messed up by someone else. When it’s your turn again, pick up where you left off. Everything will be right where you left it.
  • Order your Acer C7 Chromebook here.

2.3 Chrome OS Computers

2.3.1 Google Pixel

The newest Chromebook is Google Pixel with touch screen and high resolution display. Read more about Google Pixel here.

item.title: (LSJ) Federal Government Regulation of AI
item.content:encoded:
excerpt from Joel Nantais entry on Medium. Read the entry here.

Regulation of Artificial Intelligence: The Americas and the Caribbean

What are they proposing to be the most important considerations of AI rules?

  1. Public Trust in AI. Any government regulation of public sector AI must encourage “reliable, robust, and trustworthy AI” and these standards should be the overarching guiding theme.

  2. Public Participation. Agencies should leverage existing mechanisms and requirements to allow for public oversight and participation in any AI regulations or rules. The hope here, as underpins much of the APA, is that the public will voice concerns and share information not considered internally by the government agencies that will reshape the regulations.

  3. Scientific Integrity and Information Quality. The draft rules require agencies to engage with, and rely on, quality scientific research and information when designing regulations on AI. It also requires transparency of this research to allow for updated or contradictory information to be presented. The gets to the heart of the requirements for validity standards for AI models.

  4. Risk Assessment and Management. The draft rules require agencies to approach AI regulations from a risk-based approach. This acknowledges there will be imperfection in AI, but allows for context-based risk assessments in regulation. Therefore, some risks are acceptable if they allow AI to progress in line with the overarching goals, but AI which pose “unacceptable harm, or harm with greater harm than benefits” can be regulated.

  5. Benefits and Costs. A long theme in regulation requires agencies to only pursue rules if the intended benefits of the regulations outweigh the costs of them. This must be true in AI regulations according to the draft rules.

  6. Flexibility. The draft rules require that agencies regulate AI in a way that is flexible to accommodate rapid growth and changes in AI. This should be accomplished by focusing on performance-based regulation, rather than design-based. This means that rules will not dictate “how”, but rather will focus on the “what” of AI.

  7. Fairness and Non-Discrimination. Importantly, the focus of regulations in this area highlights the need for agency regulations to ensure fairness and non-discrimination in accordance with existing laws and rules only. Additionally, the focus should be on the outcomes of the AI decisions and and unintended discrimination compared to existing processes as a baseline.

  8. Disclosure and Transparency. The requirements for regulations of transparency under the draft must be “context based”. The context must consider potential harms, the magnitude of those harms, technical state of the AI, and the potential benefits of the AI. This is an interesting assessment for regulations as it allows for a number of subjective determinations for agencies to consider when determining whether or not o require transparency of AI in the private sector.

  9. Safety and Security. Under this section, agency regulations must focus on the controls over confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the data used in an AI application. The goal is to ensure private sector resilience and protection against attack and exploitation by bad actors.

  10. Interagency Coordination. And the final requirement of the OMB draft rules is to ensure sharing and commonalities between agencies’ regulations. This will be enforced through interagency review of draft regulations before they are made publicly available.

item.title: (LSJ) Miten voin rakentaa robotin joka pitää huolta puutarhastani käyttäen Google Cloudin tarjoamia palveluja?
item.content:encoded:
Miten voisi rakentaa robotin joka pitää huolta puutarhastani käyttäen Google Cloudia?


Tässä on muutamia vaiheita, joiden avulla voit rakentaa robotin, joka pitää huolta puutarhastasi käyttäen Google Cloudin tarjoamia palveluja:

  1. Suunnittele robotti. Mitä toimintoja robotin tulisi suorittaa? Mitkä ovat sen mitat ja paino? Mitä sensoreita ja aktuaattoreita se tarvitsee?

  2. Luo robotti. Voit rakentaa robotin itse tai ostaa sen valmiina. Jos rakennat sen itse, sinun on valittava sopivat osat ja koodattava robotin ohjausjärjestelmä.

  3. Yhdistä robotti Google Cloudiin. Voit käyttää Google Cloud Platformin IoT Core -palvelua robotin yhdistämiseen pilveen. IoT Core tarjoaa yhteyden robotin ja pilven välillä sekä auttaa sinua keräämään ja analysoimaan robotin tuottamia dataa.

  4. Luo robotin älykkyys. Voit käyttää Google Cloud Machine Learning -palvelua robotin älykkyyden luomiseen. Machine Learning voi auttaa sinua tunnistamaan robotin havaitsemat objektit ja tekemään päätöksiä niiden perusteella.

  5. Testaa robotti. Kun robotti on valmis, sinun on testattava se huolellisesti, jotta varmistat sen toimivan oikein.

Tässä on muutamia erityisiä Google Cloudin palveluja, joita voit käyttää robotin rakentamisessa ja käytössä:

  • IoT Core: Yhdistää robotti pilveen ja auttaa sinua keräämään ja analysoimaan robotin tuottamia dataa.

  • Machine Learning: Luo robotin älykkyyden.

  • Cloud Storage: Säilyttää robotin tuottamaa dataa.

  • Cloud Functions: Suorittaa robotin ohjauslogiikkaa.

  • Cloud Vision: Tunnistaa robotin havaitsemat objektit.

Tässä on esimerkki siitä, kuinka voit käyttää Google Cloudin palveluja robotin rakentamisessa:

Robotti voisi käyttää IoT Corea kerätäkseen tietoja sen antureista, kuten kamerasta, laserista ja paineanturista. Tämä data tallennettaisiin Cloud Storageen. Cloud Functions voisi suorittaa robotin ohjauslogiikkaa, joka perustuisi Machine Learningin tuottamiin tietoihin. Cloud Vision voisi auttaa robottia tunnistamaan kasveja ja muita objekteja sen ympäristössä.

Tämä on vain yksi esimerkki siitä, kuinka voit käyttää Google Cloudin palveluja robotin rakentamisessa. Voit käyttää erilaisia palveluja ja ottaa käyttöön erilaisia ominaisuuksia tarpeidesi mukaan.

Mitä erilaisia robotinvalmistajia Google Cloudin kanssa olisi helpointa käyttää jos haluaa rakentaa puutarhasta huolehtivan robotin?

Tässä on muutamia robotinvalmistajia, joiden robotit ovat yhteensopivia Google Cloudin kanssa:

  • Arbotix: Arbotix on avoimen lähdekoodin robottisarja, joka on suunniteltu helppokäyttöiseksi ja moduuliksi. Arbotix-robotteja voi käyttää monenlaisten tehtävien suorittamiseen, mukaan lukien puutarhanhoito.

  • OpenBot: OpenBot on toinen avoimen lähdekoodin robottisarja, joka on suunniteltu helppokäyttöiseksi ja edulliseksi. OpenBot-robotteja voi käyttää monenlaisten tehtävien suorittamiseen, mukaan lukien puutarhanhoito.

  • Robotis: Robotis on yritys, joka valmistaa ammattimaisia robotteja. Robotis-robotteja voi käyttää monenlaisten tehtävien suorittamiseen, mukaan lukien puutarhanhoito.

Nämä robotinvalmistajat tarjoavat valmiita robotteja, jotka ovat yhteensopivia Google Cloudin kanssa. Voit myös rakentaa omia robottejasi käyttäen näiden valmistajien komponentteja.

Seuraavassa on muutamia vinkkejä puutarhasta huolehtivan robotin rakentamiseen:

  • Aloita pienestä ja yksinkertaisesta robotista. Älä yritä rakentaa liian monimutkaista robottia ensimmäisellä kerralla.

  • Käytä avoimen lähdekoodin robottisarjaa. Avoimen lähdekoodin robottisarjat tarjoavat enemmän joustavuutta ja räätälöintimahdollisuuksia.

  • Opettele robottien ohjelmoinnista ja toiminnasta. Mitä enemmän tiedät roboteista, sitä helpompi on rakentaa ja käyttää niitä.

Toivottavasti näistä vinkeistä on apua puutarhastasi huolehtivan robotin rakentamisessa.

item.title: (LSJ) what are business cases that combine blockchain and LLMs?
item.content:encoded:
Blockchain technology has several use cases in the legal industry, including smart contracts, land registry, intellectual property rights, chain of custody, and more

17

Enterprise Lawyers can leverage blockchain Technology to streamline and simplify their transactional work, digitally sign and immutably store legal agreements.

Using scripted text, smart contracts, and automated contract management reduces excessive time spent preparing, personalizing, and maintaining standard law documents, and these cost savings are passed on to the customer after profit.

Additionally, blockchain-based public ledgers offer a new form of property rights management, which allows for a measurable reduction in transaction costs.

Therefore, combining LLM and blockchain technology could hypothetically create secure, private, and user-controlled digital identity solutions, and users might be able to authenticate their identities seamlessly.

Perplexity.ai

item.title: (FP) CORDIS explains EUs FP7
item.content:encoded:
7th Framework Programme (FP7)

The Seventh Framework Programme for research and technological development (FP7) is the European Union´s chief instrument for funding research over the period 2007 to 2013. CORDIS is the official portal for participating in FP7 and following related developments in European science and technology.

Network of National Contact Points (NCPs)

The network of National Contact Points is the main structure to provide guidance, practical information and assistance on all aspects of participation in FP7.

What is the NCP network?

NCPs are national structures established and financed by governments of the 27 EU member states and the states associated to the framework programme. NCPs give personalised support on the spot and in proposers’ own languages.


The NCP systems in the different countries show a wide variety of architectures, from highly centralised to decentralised networks, and a number of very different actors, from ministries to universities, research centres and special agencies to private consulting companies. This reflects the different national traditions, working methodologies, research landscapes and funding schemes.

 

Lifetime Oy Ltd. is member of the CORDIS Network.

item.title: (FP) European Commission proposes new strategy to address EU critical needs for raw materials
item.content:encoded:
Brussels, 4th November 2008

European Commission proposes new strategy to address EU critical needs for raw materials

Raw materials are an essential part of both high tech products and every-day consumer products. European industry needs fair access to raw materials both from within and outside the EU. For certain high tech metals, the EU has a high import dependency and access to these raw materials is getting increasingly difficult. Many resource-rich countries are applying protectionist measures that stop or slow down the export of raw materials to Europe in order to help their downstream industries. Many European producers suffer from such practices. On top of this, some emerging countries are becoming very active in resource-rich countries, particularly in Africa, with the aim of securing a privileged access to raw materials. If Europe does not act now, European industry is put at a competitive disadvantage. In response to this challenge, the European Commission launched today a new integrated strategy which sets out targeted measures to secure and improve the access to raw materials for EU industry.

Vice-President Verheugen, Commissioner for Enterprise and Industry, said: “We must act, to ensure that access to raw materials for enterprises will not be hampered. We need fair play on external markets, a good framework to foster sustainable raw materials supply from EU sources as well as improved resource efficiency and more use of recycling. It is our aim to make sure that Europe’s industry will be able to continue to play a leading role in new technologies and innovation. I have agreed with my colleagues, notably Cathy Ashton, Benita Ferrero-Waldner, Louis Michel and Stavros Dimas, to closely cooperate to implement the proposed strategy.”.”

Raw materials are essential for many products manufactured in Europe. In the making of a mobile phone for instance, 40 different raw materials are used, like lithium, tantalum, cobalt and antimony, all of them more and more difficult to get. A computer or television screen contains the same metals. A computer actually consists of about 60 raw materials, some of which are not to be found in Europe. As well because of rising demand from for instance China and India, these materials have gone up in price.

Despite recent price falls, raw material prices are still very high from a historical perspective. This provides a window of opportunity for new raw material projects within the EU. However, the current EU framework conditions are making it difficult to seize these new possibilities.

Recycling presents a huge opportunity to reduce import dependency for raw materials. However, many end-of-life products are illegally shipped outside the EU and are hence not recycled within in the EU.

The Commission recommends that the EU will define critical raw materials. And to give itself an integrated strategy, based on 3 major pillars

  1. Access to raw materials on world markets at undistorted conditions
  2. The right framework to foster sustainable supply of raw materials from EU sources
  3. Increase resource efficiency and promoting recycling in the EU

Read more at http://europa.eu/rapid/pressReleasesAction.do?reference=IP/08/1628&format=HTML&aged=0&language=EN&guiLanguage=en

item.title: (FP) Kuinka estää ilmastonmuutos yhdessä?
item.content:encoded:
Uudet teknologiat ovat tärkeitä ilmastonmuutoksen estämistyössä. Lifetime Oy:ssä mietimme kuinka meidän toimintamme voisi vähentää asiakasyrityksiemme päästöjä ja näin vähentää ilmastonmuutoksen nopeutta.

Web 2.0 teknologiat ovat parhaimmillaan erilaisten läsnäoloa vaativien palvelujen toteutusprojekteissa. Luomalla palveluja jotka lisäävät businesten ja yritysten välistä kommunikaatiota ja luottamusta eri arvoketjun toimijoiden välillä voidaan fyysistä matkustamista vastaavasti vähentää.

Matkustamisen vähentäminen on eräs keino vähentää päästöjä ja näin luoda terveellisempää tulevaisuutta.

Uudet Nk. Ubiquitous Computing läsnäoloon perustuvat palvelut mahdollistavat asiakkaan sijaintipaikan perusteella tarjota parhaita palveluja lokaalisti ja sieltä missä asiakas on. Tavaroiden hankinnan ja tuotannon läheisyys taas vähentää logistisia kustannuksia ja tätä kautta päästöjä. Asiakas arvostaa vihreyttä myös tuotteen valmistusprosessissa.

Lifetime Oy Ltd. on sitoutunut uuden teknologian käyttöönottoon ja palvelukonsultoinnin tarjoamiseen. Olemme erikoistuneet asiantuntijapalveluihin sekä näihin liittyviin palveluihin ja teknologioihin.

Uskomme että uusi Enterprise 2.0 aloite tulee muuttamaan Facebookin läsnäolon aidoksi liiketoiminnaksi josta hyötyvät asiakkaat, arvoketjun toimijayritykset, ja lopulta myös koko maailma.

Ota yhteyttä niin mietitään yhdessä miten uusi web teknologia voi olla osaltaa muuttamassa yrityksenne imagoa ja brandeja entistäkin ympäristöystävällisiksi.

Espoossa 28.4.2008

Risto Päärni
toimitusjohtaja
Lifetime Oy Ltd.

item.title: The Project Plan for Software Engineering
item.content:encoded:
Hello,

 

I like the brain metaphore used for some scientists (add links to this if you have them) to understand Twine’s importance and usefulness for me.

 

There is Episodes and there is Semantic Data.

 

The Episodes include story with beginning some story and a end.

 

Episode’s story include links and connected people, data in all forms. For my Beta, Twine has been at its best with Semantic Data follow-up. I have not yet learned to use Twine for creating Episode Stories as well. Nor it is necessary at the moment.

 

I created a Ruby on Rails Twine which has been great assistance for learning Programming. This Twine I prefer to keep private (as is the learning experience). The Episode of Learning Ruby is then explained in Flow is the Pay (FP) Blog in my site www.lifetime.fi.

 

Unfortunately I cannot use Twine beta version to publish Twine for Blog readers yet. If demand raises it could be subscription based , even with a small pay?

 

The results of learning Ruby on Rails ‘project’ result to a application that will be hosted and open to public later on(The next Digg f.e.).

 

From Learning Assistant Ruby Twine and Flow is the Pay Blog I move on to The next Episode of creating web 3.0 success story (application or site). Again the Story of this episode sits best to a new blog.

 

I think I need all the cool Web 2.0 resources to make things happen. Find people from Facebook, Linkedin, Twitter. Find Semantic Data from Whitepapers etc. Everything matter.

 

Twine is among the best following and creating my Lifetime Episodes, next web 3.0 applications, and most importantly communicating with you!

 

Your feedback is appreciated,

 

Have a nice day,

Risto

item.title: Hankinnat.fi
item.content:encoded:
Julkiset hankinnat Hankinnat.fi palvelusta

Suomen valtio, kunnat ja seurakunnat hankkivat tarvikkeita, tavaroita ja erilaisia palveluja tai teetättävät rakennushankkeita vuosittain yhteensä reilun 25 miljardin (2008) euron arvosta.

Julkiset hankinnat voidaan jakaa kansallisiin ja EU-hankintoihin hankinnan kokonaisarvon mukaan.

EU-hankintoja ovat kaikki arvoltaan EU-kynnysarvon ylittävät tavarahankinnat ja rakennusurakat sekä liitteen A mukaiset ensisijaiset palveluhankinnat.

Julkisten hankintojen tekemistä sääntelevät Suomessa kansalliset hankintalait.
Euroopan Unionissa hankintoja sääntelevät EUROPA Public Procurement hankintadirektiivit.

Pääperiaatteena julkisissa hankinnoissa on avoimuus, tasapuolisuus, ehdokkaiden ja tarjoajien syrjimätön kohtelu sekä julkisuus.

Kun hankintayksikkö tekee hankintoja, sen on käytettävä hyväksi olemassa olevat kilpailumahdollisuudet. 

Koska julkisia hankintoja säädellään tarkoin lailla, julkisen hankinnan toteuttaminen noudattaa aina pääpiirteittäin samaa  hankintaprosessia.

Hankinnat.fi -sivulla on tarjolla tietoa julkisten hankintojen hyvistä käytännöistä.

 

EUROPA (EU PUBLIC PROCUREMENT)

 

 

Public procurement, or 16.3% of the Community GDP, is an important sector of the European economy. The harmonisation of procedures for concluding contracts is a major achievement of the Internal market. European legislation has encouraged competition between firms by means of transparent selection procedures. It also makes provision for redress procedures against awarding authorities who do not fulfil their obligations.

European directives are being reviewed with a view to simplifying the existing legal framework and encouraging the use of electronic procedures. The summary sheets give more extensive information on European legislation on public procurement.

At international level, public procurement is exempt from the basic rules of the World Trade Organisation. In addition to the Community, 12 countries have signed the WTO agreement on government procurement (GPA).

The following links provide more detailed information on public procurement.

 Access to information

 Financing

 Public procurement in member states

item.title: (FP) Flow is the Pay as Lifetime Studios Production Strategy
item.content:encoded:
So what this one-liner Flow is the Pay really mean here at the Lifetime Studios?



<p> Let me shed some light for the catchy rhyme. The Pay part came when my friend Eric  called me and said “Risto, you have to find your pay”. One started to wonder the phrase, “so how does Eric make his pay?”. The answer is easy, as he is full-time professional in the music industry, his pay comes in the purest form from the flow if the music, i.e. when he plays guitar to his audiences. The flow of music is then distributed Online in live performances, or through digital productions end products, like Blue-ray discs, or iTunes shopping experiences to delight us music lovers.</p>

item.title: (FP) Royal Shakespeare Company Top 10
item.content:encoded:
Below is an 06/2025 updated list of the biggest TV stars associated with the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), including their notable TV roles, significant RSC stage roles, and now their major movie roles. The actors are selected based on their prominence in television and confirmed RSC performances, with major movie roles drawn from their most iconic or critically acclaimed films. The list maintains the original order and context, integrating movie roles to provide a comprehensive view of their careers across stage, TV, and film.

Notable TV Stars with RSC, TV Roles, RSC Roles, and Major Movie Roles

1. David Tennant

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - The Tenth Doctor in *Doctor Who* (2005–2010, 2013, 2023)

     - Alec Hardy in *Broadchurch* (2013–2017)

     - Crowley in *Good Omens* (2019–present)

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - Hamlet in *Hamlet* (2008)

     - Richard II in *Richard II* (2013)

     - Touchstone in *As You Like It* (1996)

     - Romeo in *Romeo and Juliet* (2000)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - Barty Crouch Jr. in *Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire* (2005)

     - John Knox in *Mary Queen of Scots* (2018)

     - Lord Asriel in *The Golden Compass* (2007)

   - **Details**: Tennant’s *Hamlet* was a critical triumph, adapted for BBC, while his *Harry Potter* role as a Death Eater showcased his versatility. His film roles, though fewer than TV, complement his RSC and TV prominence.

2. **Patrick Stewart**

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - Captain Jean-Luc Picard in *Star Trek: The Next Generation* (1987–1994) and *Star Trek: Picard* (2020–2023)

     - Charles Xavier in *X-Men* TV adaptations and related media

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - Mark Antony in *Antony and Cleopatra* (1978, Olivier Award)

     - Othello in *Othello* (1997)

     - Claudius in *Hamlet* (2008)

     - Prospero in *The Tempest* (1995, 2006)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - Charles Xavier in *X-Men* series (2000–2017, including *X-Men*, *X2*, *Days of Future Past*)

     - Captain Jean-Luc Picard in *Star Trek: First Contact* (1996) and other *Star Trek* films

     - Gurney Halleck in *Dune* (1984)

   - **Details**: Stewart’s 27-year RSC tenure underpins his iconic *Star Trek* and *X-Men* film roles, blending Shakespearean gravitas with sci-fi stardom.

3. **Judi Dench**

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - Jean Pargetter in *As Time Goes By* (1992–2005)

     - Miss Matty Jenkyns in *Cranford* (2007–2009)

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - Lady Macbeth in *Macbeth* (1976)

     - Adriana in *The Comedy of Errors* (1962)

     - Titania in *A Midsummer Night’s Dream* (1962)

     - Roles in *All’s Well That Ends Well* (2003), *The Winter’s Tale* (2015)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - M in *James Bond* series (1995–2015, including *GoldenEye*, *Skyfall*)

     - Queen Victoria in *Victoria & Abdul* (2017)

     - Queen Elizabeth I in *Shakespeare in Love* (1998, Oscar for Best Supporting Actress)

     - Philomena Lee in *Philomena* (2013)

   - **Details**: Dench’s RSC legacy pairs with her commanding film presence, particularly as M in eight *Bond* films and her Oscar-winning role in *Shakespeare in Love*, reflecting her Shakespearean roots.

4. **Ian McKellen**

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - Walter in *Vicious* (2013–2016)

     - Guest roles in *Coronation Street* (2005)

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - King Lear in *King Lear* (2007)

     - Macbeth in *Macbeth* (1976)

     - Romeo in *Romeo and Juliet* (1976)

     - Coriolanus in *Coriolanus* (1984)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - Gandalf in *The Lord of the Rings* trilogy (2001–2003) and *The Hobbit* trilogy (2012–2014)

     - Magneto in *X-Men* series (2000–2014)

     - Richard III in *Richard III* (1995, also producer)

   - **Details**: McKellen’s *King Lear* was a landmark, while his *Gandalf* and *Magneto* roles made him a global film icon, with *Richard III* directly tying to his RSC Shakespeare expertise.

5. **Kenneth Branagh**

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - Kurt Wallander in *Wallander* (2008–2015)

     - Roles in *Fortunes of War* (1987)

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - Henry V in *Henry V* (1984)

     - Romeo in *Romeo and Juliet* (1983)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - Henry V in *Henry V* (1989, also director)

     - Benedick in *Much Ado About Nothing* (1993, also director)

     - Hercule Poirot in *Murder on the Orient Express* (2017), *Death on the Nile* (2022), *A Haunting in Venice* (2023, also director)

   - **Details**: Branagh’s RSC roles launched his career, leading to his acclaimed Shakespeare film adaptations. His *Poirot* films and *Wallander* TV role highlight his versatility as actor and director.

6. **Helen Mirren**

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - Jane Tennison in *Prime Suspect* (1991–2006)

     - Elizabeth II in *Elizabeth I* (2005)

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - Rosalind in *As You Like It* (1968, adapted for BBC in 1978)

     - Cleopatra in *Antony and Cleopatra* (1982)

     - Cressida in *Troilus and Cressida* (1968)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - Queen Elizabeth II in *The Queen* (2006, Oscar for Best Actress)

     - Cesárea in *The Mosquito Coast* (1986)

     - Alma Reville in *Hitchcock* (2012)

     - Maria Altmann in *Woman in Gold* (2015)

   - **Details**: Mirren’s RSC training informed her commanding *Prime Suspect* and *The Queen* performances, with her Shakespearean roles like Cleopatra showcasing her stage prowess.

7. **Sam Heughan**

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - Jamie Fraser in *Outlander* (2014–present)

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - Macbeth in *Macbeth* (announced for 2025)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - Alexander in *The Spy Who Dumped Me* (2018)

     - Tom Buckingham in *SAS: Red Notice* (2021)

     - Jimmy Dalton in *Bloodshot* (2020)

   - **Details**: Heughan’s *Outlander* fame precedes his RSC debut, with his action-oriented film roles showing a different facet from his upcoming Shakespearean *Macbeth*.

8. **Ncuti Gatwa**

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - The Fifteenth Doctor in *Doctor Who* (2023–present)

     - Eric Effiong in *Sex Education* (2019–2023)

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - Valentine in *The Two Gentlemen of Verona* (2025)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - Ken in *Barbie* (2023)

     - The Artist in *The Last Letter from Your Lover* (2021)

   - **Details**: Gatwa’s breakout TV roles and his vibrant *Barbie* performance align with his RSC debut, marking him as a rising star across media.

9. **Christopher Eccleston**

   - **Notable TV Roles**:

     - The Ninth Doctor in *Doctor Who* (2005)

     - Maurice Scott in *The Leftovers* (2014–2017)

   - **RSC Roles**:

     - Macbeth in *Macbeth* (2018)

   - **Major Movie Roles**:

     - Malekith in *Thor: The Dark World* (2013)

     - Raymond Calitri in *Gone in 60 Seconds* (2000)

     - Major Henry West in *28 Days Later* (2002)

   - **Details**: Eccleston’s intense *Doctor Who* and *Macbeth* roles pair with gritty film performances, showcasing his range from RSC stage to blockbuster films.

10. **Anthony Hopkins**

    - **Notable TV Roles**:

      - Dr. Robert Ford in *Westworld* (2016–2018)

      - Roles in TV movies like *The Bunker* (1981)

    - **RSC Roles**:

      - Coriolanus in *Coriolanus* (1977)

      - King Lear in *King Lear* (1986)

    - **Major Movie Roles**:

      - Dr. Hannibal Lecter in *The Silence of the Lambs* (1991, Oscar for Best Actor)

      - Odin in *Thor* series (2011–2017)

      - Richard Nixon in *Nixon* (1995)

      - Anthony in *The Father* (2020, Oscar for Best Actor)

    - **Details**: Hopkins’ RSC roles in the 1970s–1980s complement his legendary film career, with *Hannibal Lecter* and *The Father* defining his cinematic legacy.

### Notes

- **Selection Criteria**: The list retains the original actors, chosen for their TV prominence and RSC involvement, with movie roles selected for critical acclaim, commercial success, or cultural impact. Films like *Harry Potter*, *Lord of the Rings*, and *James Bond* reflect blockbuster appeal, while roles like Dench’s in *Shakespeare in Love* tie to their Shakespearean roots.

- **RSC Context**: The RSC’s training and performances often shape actors’ film and TV work, with many (e.g., Branagh, McKellen) adapting Shakespeare for the screen.

- **Limitations**: “Major” movie roles are subjective; this list prioritizes iconic or award-winning performances. Some actors (e.g., Heughan, Gatwa) have fewer film roles due to their TV focus but are included for their RSC and TV significance. Sources include IMDb, Backstage, London Theatre, and X posts for recent RSC announcements.

- Verification No discrepancies were found in cross-referencing RSC roles, TV, and film credits across sources like IMDb and theatre archives.

This 04.06.25 updated list highlights the remarkable crossover of RSC actors into major TV and film roles, showcasing their versatility across Shakespearean stage, television, and cinema. If you need more details on specific roles or additional actors, let me know!

item.title: i2010 - A European Information Sosiety for growth and employment promises a better quality of life for Europeans
item.content:encoded:
i2010 - A European Information Society for growth and employment

 

i2010 is the EU policy framework for the information society and media. It promotes the positive contribution that information and communication technologies (ICT) can make to the economy, society and personal quality of life.

The i2010 strategy has three aims:

  • to create a Single European Information Space , which promotes an open and competitive internal market for information society and media services,

  • to strengthen innovation and investment in ICT research ,

  • to support inclusion, better public services and quality of life through the use of ICT.

To achieve those aims there are various actions such as regulation, funding for research and pilot projects, promotion activities and partnerships with stakeholders.

The strategy and actions, presented in the i2010 Communication of 2005, are reviewed and updated through i2010 Annual Reports. The annual report also analyses developments in the ICT sector and assesses the Member States' progress in implementing their ICT objectives.

Moreover, i2010 is currently undergoing a mid-term review to make sure that it remains up to date with the rapidly changing ICT environment. The updated strategy will be presented in spring 2008.

item.title: Internet advertising strategy at Lifetime Oy Ltd.
item.content:encoded:
Some terms clarifications for backgrounder

  • Open rate: email marketing messages sent and opened per cent rate.
  • Click-through rate (CTR): opened ads  or email messages leading user clicking and opening desired page.
  • Conversion: click versus purchase rate. Pull-in rate that show how many clicks are needed for 1 shopping experience. 1% is already good figure.
  • (PPC): Pay Per Click: In Internet Advertising you pay per clicked add the amount agreed in the campaign.
  • An AD conversion rate measures the success and return on investment (ROI) of a company's pay per click (PPC) advertising campaign. The more paid search bid prices increase, the more  product net profit is eaten in sales phase.
  • Example: Product price € 39.95 , -PPC 100 x 0.10=10 €, production costs 15 € = net profit € 14.95.

item.title: Brand Beagle Summer 2007
item.content:encoded:
BRAND BEAGLE -

Best-of-Breed Branding News from TippingSprung

SUMMER 2007
The results are in from
TippingSprung's 2007 Brand Naming Survey

 

THIS ISSUE

TOP BRAND NAMES
Airlines: go!
Spirits: Spykes
Spinoff: Nike Tailwind

TREND 1:
PLAYING IT SAFE
Fresh & Easy Neighborhood Market

TREND 2:
Creative Spelling
CK IN2U
PEBL

TREND 3:
RETURN TO CORE BRANDS
Crayola
Macy's

TREND 4:
PHARMA GETS PERSONAL
Enjuvia
Exubera
Reconcile


= = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = =

TRACKING TRENDS IN BRAND NAMING

Choosing a name is one of the most important decisions a company can make when launching a new brand. The name is usually the one element of the brand identity that remains constant while other elements such as packaging, tagline, and even product formulation can change on a fairly regular basis.

TippingSprung has partnered for the second time with marketing newsweekly Brandweek, and polled 1,331 branding professionals about what's hot and what's not among recently released brand names. (Brandweek featured the survey in a cover story, which you can read here. For a full survey report, including detailed analysis, email us.)

AND THE WINNERS ARE ...

Respondents voted on names in 13 categories. Here are a few of the top vote-getters in TippingSprung's survey:

BEST NEW NAME FOR A LOW-COST AIRLINE. Over half the respondents (51.9%) liked go!, a discount Hawaiian airline. Its brevity, simplicity, and direct call to action seem to be the most likely reasons for the name's popularity in the survey. Clickair was a distant second with 18%.

BEST NEW SPIRITS OR COCKTAIL-MIX NAME. Spykes came in first with 33% of survey respondents, followed by vanilla liqueur Kajmir (24.9%). (The Spykes name may in fact have been too clever for its own good in the marketplace: Anheuser-Busch withdrew the product shortly after its announcement, after critics complained that it was too appealing to under-age drinkers.)

BEST NAME FOR A SPIN-OFF OR STARTUP. Nike's Tailwind was the clear favorite with 71% of the vote. Tesco's Fresh & Easy Neighborhood Market came in a distant second with 12%.

TREND 1: MARKETERS PLAY IT SAFE.

With real-word names like go!, Fresh & Easy, and Spykes earning top grades in the survey, marketers gave their votes predominantly to the names that communicated most simply and directly with consumers. This result is somewhat counterintuitive, since many branding professionals, and even more corporate IP departments, generally advise against the more simple and straightforward names, as they are often difficult to protect as trademarks. At the same time, respondents' votes may reflect their longing to use such straightforward names, in the midst of a constraining trademark-protection environment.

TREND 2: SPELLING RULES ARE MADE TO BE BROKEN.

One trick that marketers use with increased frequency is slightly misspelling a name to make it more distinctive and ownable. Spykes, PEBL, Amp'd Mobile, and Joost TV are all examples of this naming trend. And as text messaging gains popularity, it seems that spelling rules will become even more flexible, as illustrated by the high votes garnered in the survey by Calvin Klein's CK IN2U fragrance.

TREND 3: TRANSPARENCY RULES.

Mars, Crayola, and Macy's are examples of a growing trend for companies to adopt their leading brand as their corporate name (rebranded from MasterFoods, Binney & Smith, and Federated respectively). This makes sense to employees, consumers, and investors, and is likely to lead to greater marketing efficiencies over time.

TREND 4: PHARMA NAMING GETS PERSONAL.

In the realm of pharmaceuticals, soft-sounding names with feminine endings (typically "a") continue to appeal to consumers. Names like Enjuvia, Exubera, and Acomplia all have positive, easily recognizable roots - rejuvenation, exuberance, accomplishment. Of the pharmaceutical names included in the survey, it is interesting to note that the most simple, easy to remember name is Reconcile, an anti-anxiety drug for dogs from the makers of Prozac. (This may reflect somewhat more lenient regulatory requirements in the non-human drug space.)



= = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = =
ABOUT THE SURVEY:
The survey, administered in June 2007 in collaboration with Brandweek, was sent to 25,000 branding and marketing professionals. The 1,331 respondents came from companies like Kimberly-Clark, McCann Erickson, Kraft, PepsiCo, and Disney.

A full survey report is available by emailing us at TippingSprung. The report includes detailed analysis, and coverage of additional questions including what the world's first truly green car might be named and whether Apple chose wisely with the iPhone name.


= = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = =
ABOUT THE PUBLISHER
Brand Beagle is published by TippingSprung, LLC, a branding consultancy in midtown Manhattan. We welcome editorial contributions from our readers. Contact us at beagle@tippingsprung.com

item.title: iStockphoto®, iStockalypse™, and CopySpace™ Referral Program agree with Lifetime Brands
item.content:encoded:
If you have the need to take digital pictures like we here at the Lifetime Scope,
but don't know a place where to keep and sell them, here is a decent service that keeps your photos organised.
You might get some good money from Your photos and art as well.
Many professional photographers have their blogs in istockphoto.com
I have tried to spirit up staff members with a fee of 10 euros plus a hug per image delivered that could be put blogs or sites. So far new digital cameras from Canon and Picasa has been all my staff has wanted.
New Nokia Phones, like N95 with 5 mpixel camera built-in has changed the situation.
Actually I have used N95 for 4 months and camera with me all the time feels great especially when working at night. If my staff is going to get my staff more excited for digital photographing I think istockphoto has lot to offer.


From the time the clock radio goes off until we finally switch off the late night news and haul ourselves back to bed, everyone in the world swims in symbols, signs, and icons. We're all quite literally looking at images all day long.
Some of us are more involved than others with this world of pictures. Some of us make our living creating, selling and discussing images. The world needs to be represented and we're here to do it – distilling the global stock of ideas into something visual, something people will understand. It's a living and we're good at it.
But we do it for something else. Because not every image just goes past us. Sometimes, the picture makes us stop, the photograph arrests us, the drawing makes us forget what we were just doing. We've all had this struck-by-lightning moment with an image. Achieving Gold at iStockphoto is pretty cool. It means you've built an impressive collection of work and are constantly improving and expanding your craft.

item.title: Does Market Research Solutions deliver results?
item.content:encoded:
Does Market Research Products deliver great results in the internet world? Companies need to understand the world and lifestyle of The Digital Natives. As a consequence, emerging globally unified microtrends will have major impact to strategy of the company. With Market Research tools it is somewhat easier to address the need of better to understand the microsegments of the markets.

"I used Digium Enterprise Market Research tool for my Master Thesis work in 2007, and interviewed top Management Executives about their Price Management Methods and Strategy. Creating the survey was easy and took me 3 months of work. No one helped me all the way." 

Many Market Research tools today have advanced and user-friendly Internet-based research and information gathering software available to find microsegments and analyze all aspects of 4P strategy

Information is gathered through Internet surveys, SMS queries, mobile forms, telephone interviews and paper forms. The software produces presentation-ready graphics that can be easily sent to Microsoft Office programs. Many of the tools are browser-based software, making the use quick and easy.

Lifetime partners will be there for conducting market reseach in shopping centres and from the streets.

Market Research solutions address the need of defining business strategy from the results.

item.title: (LB) Visual Studio 2008 tuoteperhe uudistuu
item.content:encoded:
Visual Studio Team System 2008 -tuoteperhe uudistuu. Visual Studio Team System 2008 Development Edition ja MSDN Premium -käyttäjät saavat maksutta käyttöönsä myös Visual Studio Team System 2008 Database Edition -tuotteen.

Visual Studio Team System -tuoteperheessä Database ja Development -versiot tulevat yhdistymään samaan tuotteeseen. Tämä mahdollistaa laadukkaan ja tehokkaan ohjelmiston kehityksen käyttöliittymästä tietokantaan. Tämä etu tuodaan käyttäjille jo nyt MSDN -tilauksen avulla.

Näin se toimii

Asiakkaat, joilla on Visual Studio Team System (VSTS) 2008 Development Edition MSDN -tilauksella, voivat ladata VSTS 2008 Database Edition maksutta MSDN -palvelusta. Tämä toimii toisinkin päin, eli jos käyttäjällä on VSTS 2008 Database Edition MSDN -tilauksella saa hän maksutta käyttöönsä VSTS 2008 Development Edition MSDN -palvelusta.

Oiva aika siirtyä VSTS 2008 käyttäjäksi

Visual Studio Professional käyttäjät voivat hyödyntää tätä etua hankkimalla joko VSTS 2008 Development Edition MSDN Premium -tilauksella tai VSTS 2008 Database Edition MSDN Premium -tilauksella. Huomioi myös step-up mahdollisuudet.

Mistä bitit?

Käyttöoikeudet hankkittuaan, bitit ovat saatavilla MSDN tilaajan download -saitilta (jos organisaatiollasi on MSDN administraattori, ota häneen yhteyttä). Huom! Tuotteet (VSTS 2008 Development Edition ja VSTS 2008 Database Edition) ovat erillisiä ladatattavia paketteja, tuotteet tulevat yhdistymään pakettimielessä seuraavassa versiossa!

Miksi muutos?

Kehittäjät tekevät sekä käyttöliittymiä että tietokantaratkaisuja, eikä tiukka roolijako tässä suhteessa ole aina mahdollista. Yhdistämällä kaksi tuotetta helpotamme kehitysorganisaatioiden päivittäistä työtä. Yhdistämällä kahden tuotteet ominaisuudet kehittäjät ja kehitysorganisaatiot voivat hyödyntää edistyksellisiä toiminnalliisuuksia, kuten koodin analysointia, suorituskykyprofilointia, tietokantarefaktorointia jne, ja edesauttaa laadukkaan ja tehokkaan koodin tekemistä.

Osallistu seminaareihin, lue ja katso lisää!

Aamiaisseminaari ohjelmistojen elinkaaren hallinnasta liiketoiminnan ehdoin 5.11.2008 Hotelli Kämpissä. Lisätiedot ja ilmoittautumiset täältä

Lisätietoja aiheesta:

  • www.microsoft.fi/alm
  • VSTS 2008 Development Edition
  • VSTS 2008 Database Edition

item.title: Mobilize and Share: MOSH by Nokia Corporation adds Social Networking
item.content:encoded:
Dear Lifetime Scope Journal Friend,

Information Value chains.

Try out MOSH. The content you upload has the potential to reach millions of users in hundreds of countries around the globe.

Now there is a new way to make it even easier to find, share, and distribute your content: social bookmarking. This allows you to share your content on sites like del.icio.us, Facebook, Digg, Furl, and StumbleUpon. Just visit any content item and click on the bookmark logos in the upper right-hand corner.

Also try these tips for making sure people find and download your content:

Tagging: The more tags you add to your uploads the easier they are to find. The most popular tag searches are around device type or keywords such as "theme" or "game."

Adding a Preview Image: View and download rates are much higher for applications and games that have preview images and descriptions. Make sure to add these to make your content more attractive. In MOSH, go to "My Uploads" and select "Manage Previews" after choosing an item to edit.

item.title: (LB) LinkedIn is a Social Networking Tool for Professionals
item.content:encoded: LinkedIn is a free business social networking site that allows users who register to create a professional profile visible to others. Through the site, individuals can then maintain a list of known business contacts, known as Connections. LinkedIn users can also invite anyone to join their list of connections. LinkedIn offers an effective way by which people can develop an extensive list of contacts, as your network consists of your own connections, your connections’ connections (2nd degree connections), as well as your 2nd degree’s connections (called your 3rd degree connections). From this network, individuals can learn of and search for jobs, business opportunities, and people. LinkedIn also serves as an effective medium by which both employers and job seekers can review listed professional information about one another. LinkedIn follows strict privacy guidelines wherein all connections made are mutually confirmed and individuals only appear in the LinkedIn network with their explicit consent. Other LinkedIn features include paid accounts that offer more tools to find people, and “LinkedIn Answers” developed in January 2007. A free feature, “LinkedIn Answers” allows registered users to post business-related questions that anyone else can answer. Lifetime Oy Ltd. is presented in LinkedIn.com Business Membership Catalog.

item.title: The different roles in (B-to-B) purchase process
item.content:encoded:
Organizational buyers are affected by environmental and individual factors.

Organizational buying usually involves group decision-making (decision-making unit DMU) and sometimes referred to as the buying centre. In a such group individuals have different roles in the purchase process.

The roles can be categorized as follows:

1. Initiator: the person who first suggests making a purchase.

2. Influencers / evaluators who influence the buying decision.

3. Gatekeepers who regulate the flow information.

4. Decider who has the power to negotiate the purchase.

5.Purchaser is the negotiator for the purchase.

6. Users and groups of users of the products in question.

item.title: (LSJ) Good Sales Practices * näin parannat myyntiä
item.content:encoded:
Good Sales Practices

Gather Information

  • Browse and analyze potential client's company website. How the site has been built, how company tells about their story, offerings, productization and content. Brief analysis of a company website takes only 30 minutes.
  • Investigate how company is using interactive dialog with the Sales vs. Customer. Is there Online Presence?

  • Find and analyze company pages, eCommerce pages and company presentations in LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, Slidehare, YouTube and Twitter. Get a good understanding what the company is proud of. Use LinkedIn profiles to learn backgrounds of people you are about to prospect, lead, contact and meet f2f, negotiate with and finally close sales.

  • Create Master Data for the Lead. Use SWOT Analysis to identify Strenghts, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threads from the competitor.

  • Learn prospect company's general business mission and vision and analyze those against Your Positioning.
  • Investigate their business setup, like people, partners, owners, Marketing-Mix 7P, etc.
  • Connect to top people to learn more.

Create Sales Pitch

  • Find story from the Customer's World - Why this is important to me? (customer view).
  • Identify opportunities how you could help the client.
  • Write these ideas to your sales presentation.
  • Make Customer Storyboard and Storytelling as the Basis to your product sales.
  • Even if the ideas do not immediately resonate with the people you meet, they will get an impression that you have invested time to think their business.
  • Bigger the client opportunity, more you need to invest time to presales investigation. Listen, Read, do Market Research, use Business Intelligence, setup a Big Data & Streaming Analytics pipeline.
  • Personalize sales pitch so that is differs to various contact groups. Develop variations of Your sales pitch to several contact groups differentiated by fe.
  • his/her whole career vs. versatile industry experience,tech. savvy vs. commercial savvy (or having both),
  • international vs. domestic career,
  • one function vs. multiple functional competences,
  • Personal Character Features

Meeting the client

  • Ask the client if they want to give their presentation first that will tell about their business and potentially achievements and pain points they are facing around the topic area you are selling. Once you have heard how client tells about their business it is easier to adjust your own presentation to make it resonate with the client. Listen and learn. Do not push your own message.

Develop Your Products All-Time - Digital Design 24/7

  • Keep Your products simple, so you can quickly pivot those products that do not sell in 3 months.
  • Keep Your product catalog such that you can manage it with ease. Keep Your products available in eCommerce Store.
  • Keep Your Marketing-Mix 7P alive and updated.
  • Do not sell 'tailored' or 'projects'. Customers love well defined products.
  • (Origins of this English Entry was in LinkedIn Sales Group, updated and all-round rewritten).

Näin Parannat Myyntiä

  1. Kehitä valikoimaa koko ajan.
  2. Selvitä, mitä asiakas haluaa.
  3. Hio tuotteita loppuun asti.
  4. Vie tuote kaikkialle, missä asiakas käy.
  5. Kansainvälisty, vaikka jäisit Suomeen. Maailmalta tulee kilpailijoita tänne.
  6. Ole ahkera. Ei riitä, että tekee paljon töitä. Pitää tehdä älyttömän paljon töitä.
  7. Oivalla jotakin ostajan elämästä. Tee oivalluksesta tarinasi. Esimerkkinä Happy Socks. Miksi miehille ei ole värikkäitä sukkia?
  8. Kehitä tuotettasi tarinan pohjalta.
  9. Kun kerrot tarinan, kerrot ostajasta. "Why". Älä kehu tuotetta.
  10. Kuuntele laajaa joukkoa kun testaat ja kehität tuotetta.
  11. Älä liitä liian monta ominaisuutta "Pivot"
  12. Kaikkia asiakkaita ei voi miellyttää
  13. Levitä hyvää fiilistä! Jos olet innostunut tuotteestasi, tartuta tunne työkavereihisi, pomoosi ja asiakkaisiisi.
  14. Valitse työkavereiksi tyyppejä, joilla on erilaiset tausta ja joiden kanssa viihdyt,
  15. Muista bisnestutuista yksityiskohtia, kuten lemmikin nimi. Kun tapaatte, kysy miten koira voi?
  16. Nouse nopeasti ylös jos epäonnistut. Älä jää vellomaan asiaa.

Näin Parannat myyntiä pointsit Marina Vahtola, Erkki Izarra, Jaakko Aspara, Juhani Siren (HS 4.7.2015).

Compilation by Risto Päärni

How to Present: Share Ideas That Inspire Action

Simon Sinek, Optimist and Author
