Environmental Policy

Effective Date: February 1st, 2019

Objectives and values

Lifetime Oy and its industry brands impacts on the environment and the surrounding community as a provider of Cloud Services operating with our partner Data Centers around the Globe.

The company's aim is to provide its customers environmentally sustainable services which combine renewable energy and energy consumption quality, environmental accountability, environmental policy effectiveness.

Our policy is deliver environmentally sustainable development and services together with our customers. We respect the environment in all of our operations and grow profitably. To reach our environmental objectives we support UN Climate Accord and their principles.

The Paris and Katowice Agreement builds upon the Convention and for the first time brings all nations into a common cause to undertake ambitious efforts to combat climate change and adapt to its effects, with enhanced support to assist developing countries to do so. As such, it charts a new course in the global climate effort. Read more.

Lifetime Group’s Environmental policy complies with all environmental legislation relevant for its operations and respect all applicable laws.

  • Helps customers through use of Lifetime Group Products and Services to reduce their own environmental impact.

  • Actively reduces the environmental impact caused by our own operations by transforming and delivering digital operations and processes.

  • Encourages employees to act responsibility and actively in environmental issues.

  • In line with the Lifetime Group’s continuous improvement culture, assesses the current state of environmental impact by feedback and by the measuring the results of our actions.

  • Requires that the key subcontractors and contract partners commit themselves to operating models such as our Digital Workspace that support the our environmental policy implementation.

Lifetime Group's current environmental policy is approved by the Board of Directors.

© 2019 Lifetime Group
Environmental Notice

Lifetime Digital Workspace

Lifetime Studios heads to paperless office. All paper material is recycled. Our way of work is all digital. Lifetime Digital Workspace is our Global work space where Lifetime Group communities and ecosystems deliver their content.

Terms of Service

this site follows Lifetime Group’a Branding guidelines.

Cookie Policy

We use cookies to personalize content and ads, to provide social media features and to analyse our traffic. Some of these cookies also help improve your user experience on our websites, and assist with navigation and your ability to provide feedback.

© 2019 Lifetime Group
Privacy Notice

Code of Conduct

Effective Date: February 1st, 2019

Introduction

Lifetime Group  is committed to carrying out its business in a sustainable way. In order to promote the long-term interests of Lifetime Group and its stakeholders, the company strives to maintain the highest legal and ethical standards in all its business practices. Each employee is expected to act responsibly and with integrity and honesty, and to comply with this code and its underlying policies and instructions.

Compliance with laws

All business and other activities of Lifetime Group shall be carried out strictly in compliance with all applicable laws, and under the principles of good corporate citizenship in each country where such activities take place.

Each employee is expected to comply with the requirements of those laws and regulations that apply to Lifetime Group’s operations and to his/her job, and with the principles of good corporate citizenship.

Openness

Lifetime Group promotes openness and transparency, as well as continuous dialogue with its stakeholders, including customers and other business partners, shareholders, personnel, authorities, local communities and the media.

Lifetime Group strives to be honest and accurate when communicating with its stakeholders, and our employees shall make their statements in accordance with this principle.

Respect for human and labour rights

Lifetime Group supports and respects the protection of human rights as defined in the United Nations Universal Declaration on Human Rights. No employee is allowed to take any action that violates these human rights principles, either directly or indirectly.

Lifetime Group supports basic labour rights as defined by the International Labour Organization. In this respect, Lifetime Group upholds the freedom of association and the effective recognition of the right to collective bargaining. In the case that these rights are restricted by local law, Lifetime Group endeavours to offer its employees alternative means to present their views. Lifetime Group does not accept any form of forced or compulsory labour, or the use of child labour.

Fair employment practices

Lifetime Group promotes freedom from discrimination based on race, ethnic or national origin, colour, gender, family status, sexual orientation, creed, disability, age or political beliefs, or other characteristics protected by law. We foster equal opportunity and employees are selected and treated on the basis of their abilities and merits.

Lifetime Group does not accept any form of discrimination, harassment or bullying from its employees.

Occupational health and safety

Lifetime Group endeavours to create hazard-free workplaces for its employees, contractors, and others working in various locations by applying high standards of occupational health and safety. Lifetime Group strives to assure the safety of its products and solutions through its world-class product and solution development processes.

Each employee is responsible for complying with the safety instructions, for using personal protection equipment when required, and for reporting on any shortcomings regarding safety instructions or protection measures.

Conflicts of interest

Lifetime Group expects full loyalty from its employees. Employees must avoid situations where their personal interests may conflict with those of Lifetime Group. This means, for instance, that employees are not allowed to accept gifts or entertainment from a stakeholder, except for a gift or entertainment of a minor value given on an occasional basis, providing it does not create a conflict of interest situation.

Anti-corruption

No Lifetime Group company or any of its employees may, directly or indirectly, promise, offer, pay, solicit, or accept bribes or kickbacks of any kind, including money, benefits, services or anything of value. Such payments and favours may be considered bribery, which violates local legislation and internationally recognised principles for combating corruption and bribery.

Relationship with authorities and local communities

Lifetime Group maintains constructive cooperation with both local and EU authorities and international regulatory bodies. Lifetime Group seeks to play a leading partnership role in serving the needs of the local communities whenever possible.

Innovation and protection of proprietary information

Lifetime Group fosters and encourages innovation by its ecosystem, communities, employees, sub-contractors, and its partners in all of our operations areas.

Lifetime Group’s intellectual property is one of its most valuable assets and the patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, and other proprietary information of Lifetime Group are protected.

At the same time, each Lifetime Group employee must respect the intellectual property rights of others.

Accuracy of accounting records

Lifetime Group accounting records must be accurate and reliable in all material respects. Unrecorded funds are prohibited. The records cannot contain any false, misleading, or artificial entries.

Competition and fair dealing

Competition laws aim to protect consumers and businesses against unfair business practices. Each employee shall comply with those laws. Actions such as participation in cartels, abuse of a dominant position in the marketplace, or the exchange of price or other commercial information between competitors, are prohibited. Our employees should be sensitive to competition concerns when attending occasions where competitors, or potential competitors, can be present.

Anti-fraud

Lifetime Group does not tolerate fraudulent behaviour or activities, such as embezzlement, fraud or theft. Such violations will lead to immediate termination of employment and are subject to criminal sanctions.

Implementation of Code of Conduct

Lifetime Group takes an active approach to the application of the code of conduct and promotes its implementation through the effective communication of its contents.

We monitor and report this code to our stakeholders and legal. Suppliers and business partners must follow this code of conduct to participate in Lifetime Group ecosystem. We promote the application of this code by monitoring the actions of its suppliers and business partners. Enquiries of this code of conduct are directed to Lifetime Group’s Legal Affairs representative.

Reporting any violations to Code of Conduct, Privacy Notice, Contracting Conditions Notice

Any employee becoming aware of a potential violation of these codes must contact his or her superior and Legal Affairs representative. CEO and responsible CxO must be informed. Internal team will investigate reported chapter with discretion. We shall not take any adverse actions, as a result of such reporting, against any employee reporting in good faith what he or she believes to be a violation of this code.

Sanctions

Violation of this code may lead to a warning, termination of employment and payment sanction of damages found. Additionally, certain violations of a criminal nature can lead to legal sanctions.

© 2019 Lifetime Group
Code of Conduct

Contracting Conditions Notice

Effective Date: February 1st, 2019

See Lifetime Contractor Fact Sheet for Payments, Registration, Digital Workspace Fees, NDA, Consultant Agreement.

Our General Contracting conditions are based on IT2018 YSE and EAP. We have Consultancy Agreement and NDA that every consultant needs to be sign-On. In addition, Lifetime Digital Workspace has its own contract to employees, our partners and lifetime friends such as key customer representatives, consultants, advisory board members etc.

© 2019 Lifetime Group
Privacy Notice, Environmental Notice, Cookie Policy, Code of Conduct, Contracting Conditions Notice will be reviewed by the Board of Directors. Enquiries and Contact information: risto.anton@lifetime.fi +358 400 319 010. Thank you of being a lifetime friend !

item.title: Migration Infrastructure Cloud Transformation
item.content:encoded:
Features Overview

  

Cloud Migration

1. Develop a Cloud Strategy

Cloud Strategy should be done early and in a way that prioritizes the right business objectives and optimizes technology journey. Cost Calculators and TCO are useful for analysis when building Cloud Strategy.

2. Identify the right applications that are migrated

A full analysis of architecture, complexity and implementation is easier to do before the migration rather than after. Should Monolith be broken to microservices?

3. Choose the hybrid multi-cloud

A key aspect of optimization will involve selecting solutions and cloud platform that can help guide the cloud migration process during the transition and beyond.

Key questions include

  • What tools including security are needed per solution?

  • Can chosen architecture support public, private and multicloud environments?

  • How to scale?

  • How can it help businesses deal with complex interdependencies?

  • How to avoid lock-in and inflexible architectures and redundant and out-of-date technologies.

4. Plan early how to maintain data integrity and operational continuity

Managing risk is critical, and sensitive data can be exposed during a cloud migration. Post-migration validation of business processes is crucial to ensure that automated controls are producing the same outcomes without disrupting normal operations.

5. Adopt an end-to-end approach

Service providers should have a robust and proven methodology to address every aspect of the migration process. This should include the framework to manage complex transactions on a consistent basis and on a global scale. Make sure to spell all of this out in the service-level agreement (SLA) with agreed-upon milestones for progress and results.

Read IBM Blog entry here.

Learn more

Transformation

In the past few years, going cloud native has been a big advantage for many companies. But it’s a tough technique to get right, especially for enterprises with critical legacy systems. This practical hands-on guide examines effective architecture, design, and cultural patterns to help you transform your organization into a cloud native enterprise—whether you’re moving from older architectures or creating new systems from scratch.

By following Wealth Grid, a fictional company, you’ll understand the challenges, dilemmas, and considerations that accompany a move to the cloud. Technical managers and architects will learn best practices for taking on a successful company-wide transformation.

Cloud migration consultants Pini Reznik, Jamie Dobson, and Michelle Gienow draw patterns from the growing community of expert practitioners and enterprises that have successfully built cloud native systems. You’ll learn what works and what doesn’t when adopting cloud native—including how this transition affects not just your technology but also your organizational structure and processes.

You’ll learn:

  • What cloud native means and why enterprises are so interested in it

  • Common barriers and pitfalls that have affected other companies (and how to avoid them)

  • Context-specific patterns for a successful cloud native transformation

  • How to implement a safe, evolutionary cloud native approach

  • How companies addressed root causes and misunderstandings that hindered their progress

  • Case studies from real-world companies that have succeeded with cloud native transformations.

Learn more

Integration

Delivering excellent customer experiences is no longer a matter of differentiation — it is a matter of survival. To meet customer expectations today, an organization must facilitate seamless cross-app data sharing by integrating the many different applications the customer interacts with throughout their journey. A successful integration strategy will allow a company to generate multidimensional customer insights, anticipate customer needs, and minimize churn.

Read about RedHat Integration

Learn more

Lifetime Oy Ltd. Company Profile

Lifetime Oy Ltd. is a small-sized consultant company specialized in digital productions and Project Management, located in Helsinki, the Capital of Finland, Europe. The number of personnel is currently two full-time and a network of freelance consultants and partners.

Lifetime Oy Ltd. was established in 1989 as a result of five students creating in a start-up. The Original business idea was import trade of laptops, media products and Telecom products. We also created a Dbase IV financial application for SME.

In 1992 other partners moved to other duties while current owner of the company stayed in while shifting business focus into software production. At the time multimedia applications were sold f.e. University of Helsinki.

Lifetime Oy Ltd. export 95 % of it’s productions, it’s main export markets being in EU, especially in the Scandinavia, UK, and Germany. In spite of tough competition, the company has done very well with the newest technologies , like 2.0 applications.

The plan is to grow to 200+ consultant multi productions company in coming years.

Own innovative products are also under careful planning. Lifetime Oy’s corporate blogging flagship is Lifetime Scope Journal (LSJ), which has readers all over the world.

As to the company’s performance this year, currently in pre-seed phase of few business projects, expected net sales will be ca. 120 thousand euros for 2008-2009. The company is privately owned.

The foundation of the company’s vigorous growth is in its specialization, state of the art technology, expertise of Productions Management, focus in customer related projects, and own innovative products and services.

DWS Features Overview

The AI Features

The Machine Learning Features

Our Data Lakehouse Solution

Analytics Services

Artificial Intelligence

Learn more

Machine Learning

Machine learning is a method of data analysis that automates analytical model building. It is a branch of artificial intelligence based on the idea that systems can learn from data, identify patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.

Why is machine learning important?

Increasing interest in machine learning is due to the same factors that have made data mining and Bayesian analysis more popular than ever. Things like growing volumes and varieties of available data, computational processing that is cheaper and more powerful, and affordable data storage. All of these things means it's possible to quickly and automatically produce models that can analyze bigger, more complex data and deliver faster, more accurate results – even on a very large scale. And by building precise models, an organization has a better chance of identifying profitable opportunities – or avoiding unknown risks.

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

dws website address is dws10.com

Company website address is lifetime.fi

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where we send your data

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

Lifetime Oy Ltd. Consulting Services

 

Lifetime Oy’s Mission is to help our customers to bring their business close to the microsegmented, microtrend-oriented, digital lifestyle customer success stories.

Today, all customers are in the internet.People with digital lifestyles chat in Instant Message boards, f.e. Skype, fly and shop in the virtual worlds (f.e. Second life), game and gather new product information in the game worlds, read email and publish with their mobile phones and iPhones.Digital lifestyle people read and subscribe to business blogs like LSJ and Wall Street Journal with Kindle and Kaywa, write business plans and sign deals in iGoogle, find new friends and services in Y! Go Mobile Messenger.

Selling those paintings and books in net auctions, get rich and buy and sell stocks in India or OMXH, NYSE, etc. Above all, digital lifestyle oriented market segments lead the market, they tend to evangelize their findings in Del.icio.us or Digg, and they learn about your business and their future prospects, job openings, friends, networks, groups, and nearly all aspects that internet 1 web pages are not providing.


Your Sales is trying to catch the customer by Facebook, MySpace, Furl or next social networking, with direct contacts, arranging seminars, organizing sales meetings etc.

The ERP Approach

Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) is great thing for many business issues in Industrial Management perspective.

But where are your business processes? Does your IT manager wish, that they are running in the closed environment, in a cost centre, far away for the customers and partners?


Does results of the ERP project show a lot of costs without strategy to address digital native customer needs nor their wishes and market evolving microtrends?

What is good for from (B-to-B) perspective is not always what your customer needs.

The Customer Oriented Approach

For customers the only visible thing is your website and perhaps a product in shopping mall.

Why is that?

With Lifetime consulting services first step is to identify to whom and why you are producing those business processes.

We want to help your company to move towards new open business culture where focus is put back to the customer.

The Customer pays your salary, not the company. What is the key for better business profitablity and market share?

What is your company (B-to-C) Business to Customer Strategy?

Lifetime Industrial Services

Car Industry Business Case

Multiple Industries are open for disruptive new innovations. We are committed in Lifetime Certified Consortium providing solutions to those needs. We tailor solution teams from 61 IT Roles, 6 Skills levels, 21 cloudsourcing teams at Your Service. You get us. Advisors You Trust. Digital. Strategy. Consulting. Apps. Cloud. Streaming. Analytics. Marketing. eCommerce. AI. ML. Automation. Digital Workers and RPA. Industrial AIoT, Intelligent Autonomous solutions.

Car Industry is the leading industry in AIoT solutions. Cars has become distributed computing / edge computing power platforms where the amount of data produced per vehicle is growing rapidly while the need of managing ever more complex car ‘data warehouse’ with raising car owner demand for their vehicle.

The data collected by single car needs to be managed with Intelligent Automation (IA input) while the management platform of the car has to be in control monitoring incoming data and changes in the platform CI/CD.

  • The business development needs to predict trends, learn insight from the data collected is increasing.

  • The update intervals and the car management features toward driverless car are increasing.

  • Building monolith solutions even on cloud computing does not ensure that every car platform operates as promised (network errors, climate condition, etc.) when circumtances change.

  • Car platform needs local support teams that can be scaling up when new issue emerges.

  • Lifetime Digital workspace 2.0 Platform offers local Cloud Ready Teams Go build support, Intelligent Automation, RPA for specific car model and its platform processes that will VW want to buy from us.

Employee experience (EX)

﻿EX 1: product owners and/or program managers who need data to help drive strategies, set priorities, and unlock team potential;

EX2: development leaders who use VsM to create connected, automated, and self-governed Ci/Cd pipelines with observability for improving and accelerating the pace of delivery;

EX3: release engineers who use VsM for governance, compliance, and upstream observability to manage risk to serve these roles effectively.

Customer experience (CX)

CX: Enterprise Customers should choose for VsM solution that demonstrate both breadth and depth of functionality to support their CD out-of-the-box metrics that inform leaders on velocity, capacity, types of work being processed, and work in progress to enable leaders to create baselines and determine how well they are executing against plan. Leading vendors offers scenarios, predictions, what-if analysis to help leaders test ideas and hypotheses for removing bottlenecks and increasing throughput. other types of analytics include flow analysis and correlations between events and changes to KPis: To understand not only what changed but also what events may have caused that change, and use collected data with policies to create and guardrail automated governance and compliance. Leader EX welcome the ability to place guardrails on software development that also help speed software delivery. and automate deployment. With VsM devops, operations become the evidence that satisfies those policies.

What is AWS DevOps?

AWS provides a set of flexible services designed to enable companies to more rapidly and reliably build and deliver products using AWS and DevOps practices. These services simplify provisioning and managing infrastructure, deploying application code, automating software release processes, and monitoring your application and infrastructure performance.

DevOps is the combination of cultural philosophies, practices, and tools that increases an organization’s ability to deliver applications and services at high velocity: evolving and improving products at a faster pace than organizations using traditional software development and infrastructure management processes. This speed enables organizations to better serve their customers and compete more effectively in the market.

Project Keywords

IPMA Standard

IPMA has defined a worldwide standard for competences in the areas of Project-, Programme- and Portfolio Management. For individuals, we have defined the IPMA Individual Competence Baseline®, ICB version 4 (for free download click here); We have defined the standard for excellent projects, the IPMA Project Excellence Baseline® or PEB (for free download click here), and we have defined the standard for organisations, the IPMA Organisational Competence Baseline® or OCB (for free download click here).


Projektien sanastoa

Projekti

Projekti on määräaikaisesta organisaatiosta,  tavoitteellisesta rajattujen ja vaiheistettujen tehtävien prosesseista koostuva ohjattu kokonaisuus, jolla on etukäteen sovittu aikataulu ja budjetti.(Muokattu teoksesta projektiliiketoiminta (Artto, Martinsuo, Kujala) alkup. Lewis (1995), Prince2 (2002), IPMA(1999), PRY(2004), Risto Päärni (2008))

Projektin päämäärä

Projektin päämäärä on tulevaisuuden tila, johon projektin toteuttamisella pyritään.(Artto, Martinsuo, Kujala, 2006).

Projektinhallinta

Projektinhallinta on projektin tavoitteiden ja päämäärän saavuttamiseen tähtäävien johtamistapojen soveltamista. Se sisältää rooleina projektin ohjausryhmän, projektipäällikön, sidosryhmät kuten toimittajayhteistyön, sekä projektin työryhmät. Projektinhallinnan tietoalueina ja (osa-)prosesseina, projektipäällikön osaamisena ja ominaisuuksina, sekä projektinhallinta työvälineinä ja dokumentointina.

Projektijohtaminen

Projektijohtaminen tarkoittaa tapaa organisoida työn tekeminen projekteiksi (Pelin 2002).

Ohjelma

Suuri projekti tai yleensä usemman projektin muodostoma kokonaisuus, jolloin ohjelman projekteilla on yhteinen päämäärä. Kutsutaan myös strategisiksi ohjelmiksi.

Hanke

Sama kuin projekti tai iso projekti.

Urakka

Kiinteähintaiseksi määritetty projekti. Tarkka laajuuden määrittely, toimittajan ottama vastuu ja riski. Asiakkaan ja toimittajan suhde on selkeä.

Toimeksianto

Konsultoinnin kohteena oleva tehtävä, jonka yksi osapuoli antaa toiselle osapuolelle suoritettavaksi tietyillä ehdoilla.

Työryhmä

Tiettyä projektia varten koottu ryhmä, usein esim. osana hankevalmistelua.

Työ

Työ voi olla suppea tai laaja tehtäväkokonaisuus, jopa projektin laajuinen. Suppeana tehtäväkokonaisuutena työ liittyy projektin näkökulmaan tuote- tai työrakenteena ja vaihe- tai tehtävärakenteena.

Missio, Tehtävä

Asiakkaan strategiseen tarpeeseen perustuva missio, projektin olemassaolon tarkoitus.

Tehtävä

Projektityön suorittamisessa yksi askel projektin toteuttamiseksi.

Open leadership is both a set of values or principles (mindsets) that people embrace, and a collection of practices (behaviors) they exhibit because of those beliefs.

The aim is to use and later on certificate with ISO Standards when building our business processes and best practices, especially these are important to us:

ISO 14000 Standard family: from compassion into action

ISO 14000 Standard family shows our commitment to move compassion into action in Environmental Management, environment protection and sustainable development.

ISO 9000 Standard family: Quality Assurance Management

  • The ISO 9000 Standard family of quality management systems (QMS) is a set of standards that helps organizations ensure they meet customers and other stakeholder needs within statutory and regulatory requirements related to a product or service.

  • ISO 9001:2015 specifies requirements for a Quality Management system when an organization:

    a) needs to demonstrate its ability to consistently provide products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, and

    b) aims to enhance customer satisfaction through the effective application of the system, including processes for improvement of the system and the assurance of conformity to customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.

    All the requirements of ISO 9001:2015 are generic and are intended to be applicable to any organization, regardless of its type or size, or the products and services it provides.

Lifetime Group’s commitment to ISO 9001:2015 is a guarantee on high quality of our business practices and services.

ISO 45001 Occupational health and safety

Lifetime Group’s commitment to ISO 45001 shows that we are working to create a safe and sound workplace.

In-house Coach esimiesten valmennus

Role description : In-house Coach ketterä esimies

Valmennuksen tavoite: Kehittää henkilön esimiesvalmiuksia, tiimivalmiuksia sekä kykyä ja taitoja toimia in-house coach roolissa ketterässä organisaatiossa.

Valmennuksen taustaa: Lifetime Group tuottaa konsultteja 72 cloud sourcing and delivery rooliin. In-House Coachaus on esimiesvalmentajaroolimme jonka merkitys on lähtenyt voimakkaaseen kasvuun myös laajemmin yrityksissä.

Kyvykkäät henkilöt tarvitsevat in-house coachin asiantuntijaroolinsa tueksi perinteisen esimiehen lisäksi.

In-house Coach valmennus 3 pv

  • 1. lähipäivä In-House coach rooli sisäisessä palvelutyössä (EX employee experience) sekä valmentavan johtamisen perusteet.

    • keho / mieli järjestelmä.

  • 2. lähipäivä In-house coach rooli (CX Customer experience) asiakasjohtamisessa (LX Leadership experience) sekä sidosryhmätyössä

  • 3. lähipäivä In-house coach ja tietohallinnon organisaatiossa (OX Ownership experience) & vaikutus prosesseihin.

    • koulutus lähiopetuksena on-site sekä Microsoft Teams (ennakkotehtävät, henkilökohtainen osio)

    • ennakkotehtävät osallistujille

    • henkilökohtainen kehityssuunnitelma (kehityskeskusteluun soveltuva).

    • agile project lead and methodologies (SAFe, JIRA, roles)

    • Tooling (TX in-house coach tool experience and tooling methodologies & techniques).

    • Sisältää kirjan “Konsultin käsikirja 2021”.
